t: Byzantium was founded by colonists from Megara, traditionally in 667 BCE, on the promontory that commands the Bosporus.
It grew rich from tuna fishing, tolls and the Black Sea grain trade, and the great powers of Greece fought for its loyalty.
After centuries as an ally of Rome it lost its freedom under Vespasian; Constantine refounded it as Constantinople in 330 CE.
dyk: Herodotus tells how the Persian general Megabazus called the people of Chalcedon blind for settling on the Asian shore when the far better site of Byzantium lay opposite.
ev: Megarian colonists found Byzantium, according to tradition
A Phoenician fleet burns the city after the failure of the Ionian Revolt
Pausanias captures Byzantium from the Persians
Alcibiades recovers Byzantium for Athens after a siege
Byzantium withstands the siege of Philip II of Macedon
Tolls on Black Sea shipping provoke war with Rhodes and Bithynia
Vespasian takes away the city's freedom and annexes it to a Roman province

f.founder: Megarian colonists, led according to legend by Byzas
